notes.title: Unreal Table Ball Update One Beta 3
notes.content:
Unreal Table Ball Update One Beta 3
2025.02.23.0

Changes
Changed how the Steam Sync works

The process for syncing achievements on Steam is now Check and Unlock "free" achievements ingame -> Request Steam User Stats and Achievements -> On success Get the data for all ingame achievements -> For each individual achievement - Check whether it's unlocked -> If so, Check if unlocked on Steam -> If not, Unlock on Steam. Once every single achievement has been processed -> "Store" the stats and achievements. Originally some of the steps taking place outside of the "achievement loop" were taking place inside the loop, this likely lead to issues in Steam and so hopefully, this should fix that issue.

Updated the achievements menu.

 The individual achievement listings have been remade.

Updated the game controller

 The game should no longer, spawn bumper 1 in front of the camera in the main menu, nor try to access input.
 The issues outlined above were caused by me using the exact same game controller and "Game Mode" within the Main Menu Map and not experiencing these specific issues myself until today

Playtest Builds now use the Playtest icon.
Demo Builds now use the Demo icon.

Fixes
Fixed an issue where the game was starting with both the player and the AI having 49 points...

 When testing the issue with achievements I needed to basically force my points score to be close to the first achievements. Due to an oversight, I left this in the game... This has now been fixed.

The 3D Game Mode! - It'll be about the same as the old version
Further enhancements to the VR Mode Beta - I'll be making this live for everyone using the Playtest when it is updated.
Start of the saving system - This won't be accessible within the actual game and will mostly be hidden until it's ready. At the start the save system will be used purely for saving achievement progress.
Adding the customization system to the main menu.

notes.title: Announcing our new Beta branches
notes.content:
As part of our commitment to improving our beta process, allowing for better collaboration with the community we're introducing new Beta branches.

What are the new branches and what can I expect to find within them?
The new branches are, Canary, Alpha and Beta.

Canary - Replaces our old "devBeta" branch. This will have the most bleeding edge changes, and may be SUPER buggy. You'll get to see changes before anyone else, but updates may be lackluster in content. A new Canary build will be released every time new content is available. These builds will NOT have changelogs posted, however you can always check our Trello page to know what's currently within a Canary build and the changes.txt file will contain the most noteworthy changes.

Alpha - These are builds with a little more content then Canary builds. A new Alpha build will be released about every 2 weeks. These builds will NOT have changelogs posted, though a list of changes will be within a changes.txt file inside the game files.

Beta - These builds will be almost ready for release, but not there yet. A new Beta build will be released about once a month. These builds will have changelogs posted, and a list of changes can be viewed within the changes.txt file in the game files.

Default - This branch will contain our "release candidate" builds, these are versions of the game that are BASICALLY ready and really only need bug testing. These builds will ONLY be released if our checklist is complete and enough content is added. These builds WILL have changelogs posted, and a list of changes can be viewed within the changes.txt file in the game files.

As always you can view a list of changes and what's to come on our Trello page.

notes.title: Beta Bytes #3
notes.content:
Wow 3 Beta Bytes in 3 months ya'll must be feeling lucky.
Anyway, this Beta Bytes has some unfortunate news, but also some happy news. Lets get into it.

Good News Everyone
Settings Rework
We've started reworking the entire settings system introducing the ability for settings to save between game loads and a bunch of brand new settings. We even introduced the ability to disable content itself from existing within the game.

More UI Reworking
We're retheming and reworking our UI elements again. We're hoping that all UI are now more consistent across the board. However, as we've changed the colours of quite a few elements, we need ya'll to let us know just how accessible these new colours are. We're considering changing all Buttons to use a brighter colour to be more visible but we're not sure yet. Let us know (lockyzdev@gmail.com)
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42732853/fc6f522feb5ad7c19818ccea886f93f7de22f583.png

Started working on old Game Modes
With Beta 5 we finally add back the 3D game mode, but in a new fashion. Instead of being a full-blown game mode it's simply a toggle that changes the camera. While it isn't as good as the 3D game mode of yesteryear (can't even move the camera or move left-right) we'll be improving it and working on it as time goes on

Content Toggles
Along with the above, Beta 5 also adds content toggles to the settings menu (Main Menu only). This means you can disable features such as, skins, custom colours, Easter Eggs, survival mode, etc.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42732853/a6d5d8fd3e6bc4bfdf98bb38f0b44690f541caf5.png

Survival Mode
Speaking of Survival Mode, we introduced the first version of our Survival Mode in Beta 4. While it's basic in it's implementation right now, we're going to be working on it and adding to it. (There seems to be a theme here).
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42732853/fcc052425cedb8db2610b020c337cb1c94d15d92.png

THEMES
That's right, we started working on themes again. For now, themes only change the background present throughout the game. However we'll be expanding this feature over the future. (Remember my amazingly placed pun from before?)

And now the bad
Online Multiplayer Update
We've unfortunately made the decision to postpone the online multiplayer mode for Table Ball again. We know, we've postponed it quite a few times now. It's just not ready yet, and for a feature this big, we'd need to be testing it NOW for it to be ready and in a public build by June.

Remote Play & Steam Input
Due to how Unity works both of these features are being canned. We wanted to at least get Steam Input out in some fashion so ya'll aren't dealing with our terrible default controller scheme. Instead, you guys are welcome to send us an email (lockyzdev@gmail.com) with the subject "CONTROLLER SCHEME" with the controller scheme you'd like to see us use, and we'll consider it.

In Closing
This will HOPEFULLY be the last Beta Bytes for another month or so. We want to finish everything on our to do list for this update soon so we can begin the final beta testing round and resubmit the game for Steam Deck compatibility.

You can view the most recent changelog candidate here: https://docs.lockyzdev.net/home/table-ball-changelogs/2.0.0 (Includes information about unfinished features)

Remember, we're always accepting feedback and bug reports.
You can post bug reports here: tracker.lockyzdev.net
You can send us feedback on the Steam Forums, our Discord or by emailing us at: lockyzdev@gmail.com

Table Ball Survival mode
Do you enjoy a constant onslaught of enemies? Do you enjoy potentially dying and losing all progress?
Well then this game mode, is for you.

Introducing, Survival Mode, a new addition as of the 2.0.0 update.

MEET THE HEALER

INTRODUCING THE INCONSISTENT ENEMY

- Has a randomly selected damage amount 1-20

AND NOW THE REGULAR ENEMY

SPEEDY ENEMY TYPE

- However only does 1 Damage

How do Spawners Work?
Every Spawner has an 85% depending on the spawner chance of spawning an enemy every 2 seconds. From there the spawn has a 10% depending on the spawner chance of not being a "regular" enemy where it will pick one of the 4 types at random As the Regular type is still part of the calculation of picking a special enemy, the spawner CAN spawn a regular enemy in place of a special enemy

notes.title: Beta Bytes #2
notes.content:
Hi all, welcome BACK to Beta Bytes.

Today we're gonna talk about the current version of the beta, what we've added, what's coming next and a potential date of when we're wanting to release this version.

Money System
We added the finalish version of our paid-skins system. All skins should now cost "pings", the game will give you 1000 pings when you start the game and the deluxe edition of the game should give you an extra 1000.

In future versions earning points within the game (without cheats) will earn you x amount of pings per x amount of points (The actual ping-point ratio is currently being decided and figured out. We want to make sure it's fair and not too easy to earn pings)

Settings Save between launches
The settings system has been updated so that some settings save between game loads, this means that if for example you mute the music within the game, the music will automatically be muted when you reload the game. There are a few issues with this system right now, but we're working on it and hope it'll be finished soon.

In a future version all settings will save between loads, we're considering the possibility of saving settings to a file instead of to playerprefs so you're able to keep your settings on different machines.

Steam Deck compatibility update
Following the instructions given to us, we've updated various UI elements to be more visible on smaller screens. This means that when using the Steam Deck you SHOULD be able to see everything more clearly and won't need to squint your eyes to see it better. We've even improved controller input so that for example pressing the left/right bumpers will change pages.

There's a bit more we WANT to do to help with this, for example in a future version controller input will be enabled by default.

Bug Fixes
We've fixed quite a few bugs within the game. We've also attempted to fix quite a few more. We're hoping to make this update as bug free as possible.

Coming Soon
Online Multiplayer
We're still not ready to reveal the Online Multiplayer portions of the game. We're working on a separate branch of the game in order to update some core systems for the online multiplayer update.

Remote Play & Steam Input
We're still working on these two features. Steam Input for example will require a rewrite of parts of the bumper controller and the game manager scripts. Both of these are currently setup with Unity's default input manager which isn't designed for input editing. It's designed to be hard coded. We may even update the game so that you can customize controls... We're not sure yet, and will keep ya'll updated.

Remote Play is still not ready. It's something none of us have ever used before nor developed for. We MAY scrap using it entirely, but it's still something we're willing to try.

New Game Modes
We want to re-release the 3D and continuous game modes from the Legacy Edition. We'll be working on these soon and hope to have a beta out next month (April 2023)

Potential Release Date
We're hoping to have the next version ready for June 2023. It's a long way away, but we want this update to be as polished as possible to hopefully break the cycle of broken updates. From now on updates will happen once per quarter as opposed to once a month like we had.

Closing
Thanks for reading through todays Beta Bytes. In the future these will happen once a month (At the most).

If you would like to test the game, be sure to join the "beta test" on the games store page.

notes.title: Beta Bytes
notes.content:
Hi all, welcome to Beta Bytes.

Beta Bytes is our way of letting you guys know important information regarding future Beta testing builds. Today we'd like to talk about the next BIG update.

New Logo
We decided to dust out an older concept for the games main logo and work on it a bit more. You can view the current version of said logo on all Playtest Branding. You can view how the current version looks on the main menu below.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42732853/3a115d8aafa633f0408abd8bbb4e6555ab271799.png

Table Ball 2.0.0
The next version of Table Ball will bump the game to 2.0.0 this means that we'll be rewriting more core systems and adding lots of different features.

Online Multiplayer
Well be officially releasing the online multiplayer game mode. This will be a better version of the Multiplayer game mode from last year.

Skin Purchasing
Well release the currency and purchasing system to allow you guys the ability to purchase Skins. Well be releasing some for free. Having any Deluxe Edition of the game will grant you 10000 points on top of the 1000 the base game gives you. This currency will not be purchasable by real currency aside from that.

Steam Deck Compatibility
We recently received an email telling us about which sections of the game should be changed/improved to create better compatibility on the steam deck. We'll be following what we've been suggested and improving the game so it can be better played on all devices.

Steam Remote Play & Steam Input
We'll be working on integrating both Steams Remote Play and Steam Input APIs into the game. This way you can not only customise your controller scheme before opening the game but also so you can play the game with your online friends.

Retiring of Legacy Multiplayer and Legacy Edition
The full version will retire both Legacy Multiplayer and Legacy Edition. We only just added them but with the online multiplayer version finally being re-released we don't see the need to keep them.

When will beta begin?
We hope to start the beta sometime this month (March). Remember this is a BIG update so it will take us some time to finish it.

Fixes
Fixed bug causing the "freebie" achievement from being earnt
Fixed bug making it impossible to use touch controls

Technical Changes
Downgraded to Unity 2022.2.1f1 due to a bug. Will be upgrading again once said bug is fixed.
